objective: Change the holyagent root instructions and hooks so a root never repeats the six rule breaks in the user's failure report: writing files itself, working before the Intent exists, keeping no task list silently, narrating progress, sending an empty reply, and leaving ready work unlaunched.
requirements: User request: 'a report from a holyagent root that failed to follow the holyagent way. fix it so it never happens again!'

Failure 1: the root wrote files itself (basilismo-notes/HANDOFF.md via Bash heredocs) instead of delegating; trigger was a long pasted spec treated as prep work. Rule: edits, runs, checks go to specialists; the root's Bash is for the holyagent CLI, Git and gh.

Failure 2: the root did work before intent create and assignment create; the user's constraint ('faça para main diretamente sem prs') only reached an Intent after a correction. Rule: Intent and Assignments come first, user constraints verbatim right away.
Failure 3: TaskCreate, TaskUpdate and update_plan were missing from the session; the root kept no task list and did not tell the user. Rule: create the task list first and keep all progress in it.

Failure 4: the root narrated progress ('Preparando a especificação para os especialistas.', 'Now the content (section 10), in pieces.'). Rule: write only for decisions, blockers, acknowledgments and the final report.
Failure 5: the root answered a user message ('você não está seguindo o holyagent way') with a blank reply. Rule: acknowledge every user message.

Failure 6: after 'continue' the root created two Assignments, ran plan and ended the turn without starting the workflow, and did not return to the build task after a report was requested. Rule: start all ready independent work together and end the turn; open user objectives stay binding until done.

Observed in this session too: the holyagent CLI on Windows (Git Bash) exits 0 silently when a command reads stdin (assignment close, intent create/update with stdin), because main.ts runs Effect.runFork and Bun.stdin.text() leaves no handle keeping the event loop alive; the root silently lost a close and an intent create.

Follow .claude/CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md: instruction changes go to requirements.md first, then every model's instruction set; per-section files; Effect, JSDoc, mise run build and mise run verify passing; Conventional Commits; worktree branch and PR.
User addendum titled Addendum: workflow failures.

Failure 7: after continue, plan returned action: workflow for both Assignments and the root ended the turn without starting it; no work ran until the user complained twice. Rule: workflows run all new work; choosing this agent is the opt-in to the Workflow tool.
Failure 8: the root launched with parallel([...]) instead of pipeline(). Rule: run Assignments through pipeline(), which has no barrier; parallel() only where a stage needs every earlier result.

Failure 9: the root saved assignment dispatch output to files, printed it into context and retyped it by hand into the script as .join(newline) string arrays. Rule: pass that text as it is. Trigger: no direct route from the dispatch output to the inline script, so the root improvised one; give it a direct route.

User decision: no PreToolUse guard hook restricting the root Bash to holyagent, git and gh (the user disagrees: easy to bypass). The root already lacks Write and Edit. Name the loophole in the rule text itself (e.g. transcribing user-provided text to a file is still writing a file; delegate it).

User direction: no hooks. Levers are behavior only: (1) rule text that names the tempting exceptions (transcribing pasted content, handoff notes, scratch files and just prep all count as writing and get delegated); (2) make delegating cheaper than doing it yourself, e.g. a one-step CLI route from content or dispatch output to a running specialist, so the correct path is the path of least resistance. Removing Write and Edit does not help since Bash writes remain. The user asks for a better fix if one exists.
